subject: English
questionText:
Choose the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

Regular exercise may obviate the need for certain medications later in life.
solution:
Meaning: Obviate means to remove a need or difficulty, or to prevent something from happening.
Synonym: Prevent correctly conveys the meaning of avoiding or making unnecessary.
Other options: Delay means to postpone; Complicate means to make difficult; Replace means to take the place of.
Vocab Meanings: • Obviate: To remove a need or prevent a problem (टालना / अनावश्यक बना देना)
• Delay: To make late; to postpone (विलंब करना)
• Prevent: To stop something happening (रोकना)
• Complicate: To make more difficult (जटिल बनाना)
• Replace: To take the place of (प्रतिस्थापित करना)
conceptTested: Vocabulary and contextual word meaning replacement

questionText:
Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank in the given sentence.

It is heartening to see how many people ________ their valuable time to keep the local park beautiful.
solution:
Meaning: Give up time means to dedicate, sacrifice, or willingly yield time for a specific purpose.
Other options: Give in means to surrender or yield to pressure; Give away means to donate an item or disclose a secret; Give out means to distribute or stop working.
Vocab Meanings: • Give up: To give or sacrifice (time, etc.); to stop doing (त्याग करना / छोड़ देना)
• Give in: To surrender (हार मान लेना)
• Give away: To give freely; to reveal (दान करना / प्रकट करना)
• Give out: To distribute; to stop working (बाँटना / ख़त्म हो जाना)

questionText:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.

She explained that she was watching a movie when the incident happened.

options.A: She said, "She was watching a movie when the incident happened."
options.B: She said, "I am watching a movie when the incident happened."
options.C: She said, "I was watching a movie when the incident happened."
options.D: She says, "I was watching a movie when the incident happened."
options.a: She said, "She was watching a movie when the incident happened."
options.b: She said, "I am watching a movie when the incident happened."
options.c: She said, "I was watching a movie when the incident happened."
options.d: She says, "I was watching a movie when the incident happened."

solution:
Rule: The indirect pronoun she referring to the speaker changes back to first - person I in direct speech.

The reporting clause is in past tense (explained / said), maintaining the past continuous time frame of the background action in direct narration.

Sentence: She said, "I was watching a movie when the incident happened."
conceptTested: Conversion from indirect speech back to direct speech involving past continuous tense and pronoun shift

subject: English
questionText:
From the given options, select the homonym that corresponds to both Definition (P) and Definition (Q).
(P) To combine, merge, or unite two separate companies or organisations into one unified corporate structure

(Q) To alloy, mix, or blend a metal alloy directly with liquid mercury
solution:
Definition: Amalgamate means to combine or unite to form one organization or structure, and in metallurgy/chemistry, it specifically denotes combining or blending a metal with mercury.
Other options: Coagulate means to change to a solid or semi - solid state; Arbitrate means to judge a dispute; Consolidate means to combine multiple things into a single whole, but does not refer to alloying with mercury.
Vocab Meanings: • Amalgamate: To combine into one; to mix a metal with mercury (विलय करना / मिश्रित करना; पारे के साथ मिश्रधातु बनाना)
• Coagulate: To thicken or form clots (जमना / थक्का बनना)
• Arbitrate: To settle a dispute as a judge (मध्यस्थता करना)
• Consolidate: To make stronger; to combine (सुदृढ़ करना / एकीकृत करना)
conceptTested: Identifying a single word matching multiple domain definitions

questionText: Identify the option in which the underlined idiom has been used incorrectly.

options.A: After the startup acquired its primary competitor's patents and secured exclusive distribution rights, the board knew they held all the aces in the upcoming acquisition negotiations.
options.B: Recognising that the younger team members needed leadership experience, the senior consultant decided to take a back seat during the project, offering guidance only when explicitly asked.
options.C: The tyrannical creative director loved to lord it over his junior designers, frequently mocking their portfolios in front of the entire office to assert his dominance.
options.D: Intending to reward the ambitious young politician for his absolute loyalty, the party chairman clipped his wings by promoting him to the prestigious position of committee chair.
options.a: After the startup acquired its primary competitor's patents and secured exclusive distribution rights, the board knew they held all the aces in the upcoming acquisition negotiations.
options.b: Recognising that the younger team members needed leadership experience, the senior consultant decided to take a back seat during the project, offering guidance only when explicitly asked.
options.c: The tyrannical creative director loved to lord it over his junior designers, frequently mocking their portfolios in front of the entire office to assert his dominance.
options.d: Intending to reward the ambitious young politician for his absolute loyalty, the party chairman clipped his wings by promoting him to the prestigious position of committee chair.

solution:
Meaning: Clip someone's wings means to restrict someone's freedom, power, or ambitions.
Usage: Promoting someone to a prestigious leadership position empowers rather than restricts them, making the idiom incorrect in option (D).
Vocab Meanings: • Hold all the aces: To have all the advantages (पूरी तरह लाभ की स्थिति में होना)
• Take a back seat: To take a less active role (पीछे हट जाना / कम सक्रिय भूमिका लेना)
• Lord it over: To act in a superior, bossy way (किसी पर रौब जमाना)
• Clip someone's wings: To limit someone's freedom or power (किसी की स्वतंत्रता या शक्ति सीमित करना)

subject: English
questionText:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

The authorities have not repaired the broken roads for months.

options.A: The broken roads were not repaired by the authorities for months.
options.B: The broken roads are not repaired by the authorities for months.
options.C: The broken roads had not been repaired by the authorities for months.
options.D: The broken roads have not been repaired by the authorities for months.
options.a: The broken roads were not repaired by the authorities for months.
options.b: The broken roads are not repaired by the authorities for months.
options.c: The broken roads had not been repaired by the authorities for months.
options.d: The broken roads have not been repaired by the authorities for months.

solution:
Rule: Active have/has + not + V³ transforms into Passive have/has + not + been + V³.
Active: The authorities have not repaired the broken roads for months.
Passive: The broken roads have not been repaired by the authorities for months.
conceptTested: Active have/has + not + V3 transforms into Passive have/has + not + been + V3.

questionText:
The sentence given below is divided into four segments labelled P, Q, R, and S. Read the sentence carefully to determine which segment contains a grammatical, syntactic, or idiomatic error. Select the letter corresponding to that specific segment as your answer. (Note: Every sentence contains exactly one error. Ignore errors of punctuation, if any.)

(P) Advised by her digital marketing agent not to clap back the toxic comments / (Q) on her streaming channel, the popular gaming influencer / (R) chose instead to ignore the online trolls / (S) and focus entirely on her upcoming charity livestream event.
solution:
Rule: The phrasal verb clap back requires the preposition at when followed by an object (e.g., to clap back at someone/something).
Correction: Segment (P) must read: "...not to clap back at the toxic comments...".
conceptTested: The phrasal verb clap back requires the preposition at when followed by an object (e.g., to clap back at someone/something).

subject: English
questionText:
Electric vehicles (EVs) promise lower emissions, quieter cities, and reduced dependence on fossil fuels. However, the transition to electric mobility requires substantial investment in charging infrastructure, reliable electricity grids, and sustainable battery production. (A) ________ policymakers must recognize that technological innovation alone cannot guarantee widespread adoption. Consumer confidence depends on affordability, charging availability, battery longevity, and transparent regulatory standards.

Although EVs reduce tailpipe emissions, irresponsible mining practices may (B) ________ ecological degradation in resource-rich regions if environmental safeguards remain inadequate. Governments, industries, and research institutions must therefore develop cleaner extraction techniques and promote battery recycling and alternative materials.

If governments (C) ________ clear and consistent policy incentives, consumers would feel more confident about investing in electric vehicles despite their higher initial costs. Such confidence may encourage manufacturers to expand production and reduce prices. Equally important is the creation of an (D) ________ that rewards innovation without discouraging fair competition. Long-term industrial growth also depends on institutional credibility and predictable governance.

Ultimately, the success of electric mobility will be determined by society's willingness to invest (E) ________ a comprehensive transition that balances environmental responsibility, economic practicality, and social equity.

Identify the correct word for blank (B).
solution:
Context: The text warns about the harms of irresponsible mining practices leading to worsened environmental damage.
Meaning: Exacerbate means to make a problem, situation, or negative condition worse.
Other options: Alleviate means to lessen; Conceal means to hide; Postpone means to delay.
conceptTested: Contextual vocabulary usage and appropriate word choice for negative environmental impacts.
